newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Beazer reservations up 35 pct.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Beazer reservations up 35 pct.

text.p: Beazer Group Plc, the UK housebuilder, said on Wednesday that reservations, or new orders, for the first eight months of its financial year to date are 35 percent up on the same period last year.

Dennis Webb, chief executive, told Reuters in an interview: "The reservation trend has continued through to the third quarter. Year-on-year we are 35 percent ahead for the full eight months. Though I'd expect that to ease back slightly for the full year."
He said he expected total completions for 1997 to be up 20 percent, dampened slightly by uncertainty which may arise as a result of the May 1 UK election.

Another potential problem was a labour shortage, said Webb. The issue is of widespread concern to the industry which has cut back sharply on jobs in the years of recession since the late 1980s, only to face a squeeze now.
Asked at what point the labour shortage could become a problem, Webb said: "At the moment contracting is quiet but if it also picks up (like housing)there could be a real problem."

Commenting on the likely change of government in May, with the opposition Labour Party way ahead of the ruling Conservatives in opinion polls, he said that the industry could potentially be assisted by the release of billions of stg in capital receipts held by councils.
"This could benefit our partnership division which has had a difficult first half," he said.
But he warned that unless a future government tackled planning problems there was a danger that land prices would suffer from huge price inflation.
The price of land is a key issue for housebuilders. Beazer said it had enough financial muscle to maintain its landbank.

Webb added: "Land prices are a concern. We believe if the planning problems are not resolved we would see a spiral in land price inflation." Land price inflation is currently between 20 and 30 percent, he said, and could rise even higher.
